{
  "findings": [
    {
      "title": "High frequency of vital signs and AE assessments at every visit",
      "quote": "Vital Signs |  | X | X | X | X | X | X | X | X | X | X | X | X | X | X | X | X | X",
      "page": 46,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "Vital signs and adverse event monitoring are scheduled at every visit, including all 15 post-screening visits, which is burdensome for patients and sites, especially for a 36-week study with frequent visits.",
      "fix": "Consider reducing vital signs and AE assessments to alternate visits or only when clinically indicated, unless required for safety monitoring."
    },
    {
      "title": "Physical exam and ECG only at sparse visits may miss safety signals",
      "quote": "Physical Exam |  | X |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  | X |  |  |  |  | X | X | X",
      "page": 46,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "Physical exams and ECGs are only performed at screening, week 16, and end of study, which may be insufficient to detect treatment-emergent changes, especially for a biologic with potential cardiac or systemic effects.",
      "fix": "Add physical exam and ECG at intermediate timepoints (e.g., every 8 weeks) to align with standard safety monitoring."
    },
    {
      "title": "Ophthalmological exam only at screening and EOS may miss early toxicity",
      "quote": "Ophthalmological Exam |  | X |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  | X |",
      "page": 46,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "Ophthalmological exams are only at screening and end of study, which may be insufficient to detect early ocular adverse events, and the long gap could lead to missed safety signals.",
      "fix": "Consider adding an ophthalmological exam at an interim timepoint (e.g., week 12 or 16) to monitor for potential ocular toxicity."
    },
    {
      "title": "PK sampling at every visit is excessive and burdensome",
      "quote": "Serum REGN3500 Concentration (PK) |  |  | X | X | X |  | X |  | X |  | X | X | X | X | X | X | X | X",
      "page": 46,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "PK samples are collected at 13 visits, including every visit from week 2 to week 36, which is excessive for a monoclonal antibody with a long half-life and adds significant patient burden and site workload.",
      "fix": "Reduce PK sampling to key timepoints (e.g., trough at each dosing visit and a few post-dose peaks) to minimize burden while still characterizing PK."
    },
    {
      "title": "ADA sampling only at sparse visits may miss immunogenicity onset",
      "quote": "Anti-REGN3500 Antibody (ADA) |  |  | X |  |  |  |  |  |  |  | X |  |  |  |  | X | X | X",
      "page": 46,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "ADA samples are only collected at week 2, week 16, and end of study, which may miss early ADA development and its impact on PK and safety, especially if ADA appears and disappears between these sparse timepoints.",
      "fix": "Increase ADA sampling frequency, at least at the same visits as PK, to better characterize immunogenicity."
    },
    {
      "title": "Tight postdose vital sign window may be hard to meet",
      "quote": "30 minutes (±10 minutes) postdose",
      "page": 53,
      "section": "8.2.3.1 Vital Signs",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "The 30-minute postdose vital sign window with only ±10 minutes is tight and may be difficult to achieve in a busy clinic, especially if dosing is delayed or multiple patients are being dosed.",
      "fix": "Consider widening the window to ±15 or ±20 minutes to reduce site pressure and patient wait times."
    },
    {
      "title": "Frequent visits every 2 weeks early on are burdensome",
      "quote": "V3 W2 D15 (Day 15) | V4 W4 D29 (Day 29) | V5 W6 D43 (Day 43) | V6 W8 D57 (Day 57) | V7 W10 D71 (Day 71) | V8 W12 D85 (Day 85) | V9 W14 D99 (Day 99)",
      "page": 46,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The schedule requires visits every 2 weeks for the first 14 weeks, which is a high frequency that may be burdensome for patients and sites, especially for a chronic condition like atopic dermatitis.",
      "fix": "Consider extending the interval to every 4 weeks after the initial loading phase, if clinically appropriate, to reduce burden."
    },
    {
      "title": "Height only at screening is fine but weight at sparse visits may miss changes",
      "quote": "Weight |  | X | X |  |  |  |  |  |  |  | X |  |  |  |  | X | X | X",
      "page": 46,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "Weight is only measured at screening, week 2, week 16, and end of study, which may be insufficient to monitor for weight changes that could affect dosing or safety, especially in a long study.",
      "fix": "Add weight measurements at least at each dosing visit to monitor for significant changes."
    }
  ]
}
